search_queries: targeted PyPI and project-documentation lookups for nine named XML parsers
uncertainty: Seven verified third-party paths (lxml, beautifulsoup4, defusedxml, xmltodict, xmlschema, parsel and untangle) are selected from nine named PyPI/project-documentation leads. A bounded PyPI Simple Index search remains pending; 2 leads are unresolved, so this is not a completed top-ten ranking. lxml uses source-built libxml2 2.15.4; beautifulsoup4's documented 'xml' builder runs on the same lxml 6.1.3/libxml2 2.15.4 pins (shared parser family, no independent XML tokenizer, recover=True); xmltodict, defusedxml (guarded pure-Python ElementTree XMLParser), untangle (SAX via defusedxml's DefusedExpatParser) and the standard ElementTree path use Expat. defusedxml is a guard facade over CPython ElementTree, not an independent XML engine; its own code is constant on the valid controls, and ElementTree keeps no xmlns declarations, so its comparison with the lxml oracle omits the declaration count. untangle runs SAX without namespace processing and drops namespace URIs; its controls are checked against an lxml oracle projected to untangle's qualified-name view, not against namespace-expanded names. The lxml, beautifulsoup4, defusedxml and untangle controls exercise valid UTF-8 XML 1.0 namespace structures without DOCTYPE, not full XML conformance. PyPI Stats package downloads are not XML-specific use; Beautiful Soup downloads are mostly HTML use, and defusedxml downloads are largely transitive. lxml, beautifulsoup4 and parsel AFL feedback excludes parser.c lines 8700-8720 because address-sensitive attribute hash lookups varied across identical valid replays. xmlschema's XMLResource is not an independent XML engine: it consumes CPython's default xml.etree.ElementTree.iterparse events over the C _elementtree parser, pyexpat and Expat 2.10.0. It records xmlns declarations and per-element namespace maps itself, so its controls match the lxml path's full summary including the declaration count; its own 110 lines are the same on both controls and only their hit counts differ. xmlschema downloads are mostly XSD validation use. parsel's documented Selector(body=bytes, type='xml') is not an independent XML tokenizer: it strips the body and NUL bytes and calls lxml.etree.fromstring with SafeXMLParser(recover=True, resolve_entities=False, huge_tree=True) over the same lxml 6.1.3/libxml2 2.15.4 pins (shared lxml/libxml2 family). Both valid controls match an independent CPython pyexpat oracle. Parsel's own 100 selector.py lines are the same on both controls, so its input-dependent AFL++ feedback (209 tuples) comes entirely from libxml2 parser.c. Parsel downloads are mostly Scrapy HTML scraping use.
